title: CEITM: evaluating image-text retrieval without manual ground truth
summary: A semantic-similarity evaluation framework for image-text retrieval, used to benchmark CLIP, BLIP and ALBEF.
problem: Image-text retrieval has no reliable ground-truth method: a caption can describe many images and an image can match many captions, so one-to-one labels penalize correct answers.
approach: Designed CEITM (Cosine Enhanced Image Text Matching), which derives ground truth from semantic similarity and allows one-to-many matches instead of a one-way mapping.
Fine-tuned CLIP on Flickr8k with patch-level image resizing, contrastive loss and the Adam optimizer.
Benchmarked CLIP, BLIP and ALBEF under CEITM and compared against traditional threshold-based metrics.
results: 29% improvement in Precision@1 over the pretrained CLIP baseline.
BLIP outperformed ALBEF, which outperformed CLIP under CEITM.
Published at IEEE InCCCS 2024 and recognized with Samsung's Excellence Award.

title: Early oral cancer detection and risk stratification
kicker: Research · Capstone with Ramaiah Dental College
summary: A multi-model pipeline that highlights malignant tissue on histopathology slides and reports risk to pathologists.
problem: Pathologists need interpretable, dependable support on real patient slides, not a single opaque score.
approach: EfficientNet for cancer versus non-cancer classification, YOLO-NAS for keratin pearls and multiple nucleoli, and a second EfficientNet classifier for vascular invasion.
Combined the three findings into a risk-stratification score and a pathologist-facing report.
Curated and annotated 6,000+ histopathological images with pathologists, with augmentation for class balance.
Deployed on AWS (S3, Elastic Beanstalk with CodePipeline CI/CD, Flask, MongoDB Atlas) with encrypted patient data.
results: 99.25% classification accuracy on the collected dataset.
Published at IEEE ICSEC 2024 and presented internationally.
Second place at Ramaiah's final-year project exhibition.

title: Artificial Eye
summary: A blind-stick augmented with real-time object detection, OCR and speech output.
problem: For someone relying on instant feedback, a delayed or wrong detection is a physical failure, so accuracy and speed both have to hold on constrained hardware.
approach: Raspberry Pi 3 with an ultrasonic proximity sensor, a webcam and a speaker.
TensorFlow Lite MobileNet-SSD for detection, benchmarked against several YOLO versions.
Compared Tesseract and EasyOCR, with Google text-to-speech and Mycroft voice assistant integration.
results: The project that started a focus on applied AI with real-world consequences.

title: Multi-agent root-cause analysis for payments
summary: A LangGraph chatbot with RAG and an MCP tool server that automates log diagnostics and database lookups.
problem: Tracing a payment failure across fragmented billing systems meant manual log reading and database queries for every incident.
approach: Multi-agent LangGraph chatbot with RAG over Azure AI Search for the payments team.
An MCP server with dedicated tools per module, integrating Splunk and OracleDB.
Automated end-to-end RCA workflows so production issues no longer start with manual triage.

title: Automated payment fallout clearance
summary: A Python pipeline that detects, classifies and clears daily payment fallouts.
problem: Billing exceptions piled up daily and were cleared by hand, so the same incidents kept recurring.
approach: Python pipeline integrating OracleDB through custom SQL scripts with rule-based classification.
Deployed into the payments processing system with Docker.
results: Consistent SLA adherence for daily issue clearance.

title: Persona-based movie greenlighting simulation
summary: A multi-agent simulation of audience personas evaluating movie scripts.
problem: Greenlighting decisions depend on how different audiences would respond, which is expensive to measure before production.
approach: Scraped and cleaned 10,000+ IMDb profiles and reviews and clustered them into seven audience personas.
CrewAI-orchestrated agents simulate each persona evaluating a script across multiple parameters.
results: 60% improvement in persona-based review generation accuracy.

title: Gradly.ai
summary: A multi-agent platform that shortlists universities for applicants.
problem: Shortlisting universities usually takes counselors weeks of manual comparison.
approach: LangChain multi-agent platform with Perplexity-driven RAG over 500+ institutions.
A guided Q&A agent collects user context and generates personalized application documents through RAG.
results: Shortlisting time reduced from weeks to under a day.

title: Enterprise knowledge assistant and retrieval migration
summary: A RAG-powered assistant over knowledge bases from several business units, later moved to a newer retrieval architecture.
problem: Support knowledge was spread across business units and hard to search, and plain RAG hit a retrieval accuracy ceiling.
approach: Built an internal knowledge assistant across multiple business units' knowledge-base articles, then productized it for a client's own content across regions.
Led part of the migration from RAG to a newer retrieval architecture (OKF), rolled out wherever RAG had been implemented.
Added agentic enhancements to IT service management: resolution notes generated from work notes, chat exchanges and call summaries, with PII masked by Presidio.
results: Improved retrieval accuracy after the migration.
